req.title: Reject player creation with invalid id type
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when POST /players/ receives an id that is not an integer.
triggers: reject player creation with invalid id type

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-035 requires HTTP 422 when POST /players/ receives an id field that is not an integer for squad_number. The PlayerRequestModel defines squad_number as int; Pydantic will reject non-integer values with a 422. We need: (1) a positive case showing a valid integer squad_number is accepted (201), (2) a negative case showing a string squad_number triggers 422, (3) boundary cases for other non-integer types (float string, boolean string, null, empty string). The 'id' in the requirement title refers to the squad_number field used as the player identifier in the request body, since PlayerRequestModel has no 'id' field — id is only in PlayerResponseModel. We test exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations, and verify response body structure to catch constant mutations.

tests.name: test_post_player_valid_integer_squad_number_returns_201
preconditions: App is running in-process via TestClient
squad_number 99 does not exist in the pre-loaded database
actions: POST /players/ with a fully valid payload where squad_number is an integer (99)
expected: Response body contains firstName, lastName, squadNumber matching the request
trace: R-PLAYER-035: valid integer id accepted — positive EP partition
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_valid_integer_squad_number_returns_201():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 99,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["firstName"] == "Test"
    assert body["lastName"] == "Player"
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 99
    assert "id" in body

test_post_player_valid_integer_squad_number_returns_201()

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_numeric_string_squad_number_boundary():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Boundary",
        "lastName": "Case",
        "squadNumber": "98",
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    # Pydantic v2 coerces numeric strings; result must be 201 or 422, never 200/400/404/500
    assert r.status_code in (201, 422)
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 500

test_post_player_numeric_string_squad_number_boundary()

tests.name: test_post_player_boolean_squad_number_returns_422
preconditions: App is running in-process via TestClient
actions: POST /players/ with squad_number set to boolean true (boundary: bool is subclass of int in Python)
expected: HTTP 422 or 201/409 — boolean true coerces to 1 in Python/Pydantic; documents boundary behaviour
Status code must be exactly 422, 201, or 409 — never 200, 400, 404, or 500
trace: R-PLAYER-035: boolean squad_number boundary — bool subclasses int; Pydantic may coerce or reject
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_boolean_squad_number_boundary():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Bool",
        "lastName": "Test",
        "squadNumber": True,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    # bool True == 1 in Python; Pydantic v2 strict mode rejects, lax mode coerces
    # squad_number 1 already exists in DB so 409 is also valid if coerced
    assert r.status_code in (422, 201, 409)
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 400
    assert r.status_code != 500

test_post_player_boolean_squad_number_boundary()
